built: The file is <workspace>/kasandra/character.md, editable in any App. voice.character.start writes the starter where no file is (never overwrites) and admits it as revision 1.

Admitted with revisions: voice.character.admit {expected_sha256} admits the file as it is now only if its bytes are the ones read and it compiles; exact bytes kept in <workspace>/kasandra/.revisions/<sha256>.md with index.json (ledger.character/1). {revision: n} takes an earlier revision back as a new TAKEN_BACK revision. An unadmitted edit changes nothing; a broken edit leaves the revision in force; a damaged kept copy falls back to the starter, said in plain words. Graphite never writes your file except to start it.

Exact compile (headings ## and dash bullets, no model): Registers (plain, formal, warm, each with its kinds of work), Manner, Joining words (words only), Never say (quoted phrase or mark, with a note), Lengths (sentence words, sentences per register). Other lines and unknown headings are your notes, kept, never compiled. Errors in plain words with the line number. The file adds to the floor and never lifts it (sentence words capped at mind_words.MAX_WORDS; '!' and 0.8.6 banned words stay banned). Manner may not name the three women.

card(): the text for FRAME's system message; compile refuses a card over 160 tokens, counted by an optional exact counter (the bundled tokenizer, count=) or else by grammars.estimate (an upper estimate). Digest covers the character content only.

Governs her words with or without a model: mind_words.check() sweep and scan_text() read the character in force; API for C4's gate and FRAME: never_say(), budgets(register), register_for(kind), scan(text, register), current(), use(root), in_force(root).

Starter path is workbench/kasandra/character_starter.md (the lane table names kasandra/character_starter.md beside workbench modules), so it ships in the payload.

'Admitted' means an explicit owner press (approve scope), not automatic on read: an edit takes effect only when admitted, and an expected_sha256 guards against the file changing between read and admit.

Card limit: the compile cannot load a tokenizer, so without a counter it uses grammars.estimate (an upper estimate, about 1.3 times the real count). This guarantees <=160 real tokens but leaves only 5 estimate tokens of room over the starter; an exact count (count=) gives about 40 tokens of room. The Kernel ops pass no counter in C5 (no model); FRAME (C6) or the admit window can pass the worker's /tokenize.
The card leaves out which kinds of work go to which register (the desk picks the register with register_for), to fit 160 tokens.
